profile.reading:
Iron Mountain Incorporated (NYSE: IRM) is a publicly traded REIT headquartered in Portsmouth, New Hampshire, whose core business is physical and digital records management; its data center division was built substantially through a January 2018 acquisition of IO Data Centers. Per Wikipedia's account of that deal, the acquired IO facilities were in New Jersey, Ohio, and two Arizona sites; this registry has found no primary source tying Iron Mountain's Virginia campus to that acquisition, so it is treated as a ground-up Iron Mountain build rather than legacy IO Data Centers infrastructure.

This building, VA-2, is part of Iron Mountain's 142-acre Northern Virginia data center campus in Prince William County. Per the operator's own site, the full campus currently comprises seven operational data centers, with a planned buildout of nine to ten buildings totaling more than 2,000,000 square feet and 400-plus MW of capacity, and Iron Mountain has separately acquired an adjacent 40-acre parcel for two further buildings totaling roughly 150 additional MW.

VA-2's own address is genuinely unresolved: Iron Mountain's own dedicated VA-2 page reuses the identical 11680 Hayden Road address (and even the same Google Maps pin) published for VA-1, which is almost certainly a template or copy-paste error on the operator's own site rather than a real fact. Aggregator Baxtel separately lists VA-2 at 11660 Hayden Road, Manassas, Virginia, an address applied here as the best available figure but flagged as secondary and uncorroborated. Per the operator, VA-2 carries 36 MW of IT capacity across roughly 221,500 to 221,578 gross square feet (the operator's own pages give both figures), spread across eight data halls, and is described as the first data center in the United States to achieve DCOS Maturity Level 3, alongside ISO 27001/50001/14001/9001 and FISMA High certifications. Baxtel separately reports a 2021 opening year, not independently confirmed by this registry.
profile.capacity_note: Operator-stated 36 MW IT capacity (100% matched renewable power), roughly 221,500-221,578 gross sq ft (two slightly different figures appear across the operator's own pages), eight data halls (four at 16,650 sq ft plus four at 10,858 sq ft), described as "Tier III designed" with N+1 redundancy. Notable per operator: first US data center to achieve DCOS Maturity Level 3. Year opened (2021) per aggregator Baxtel, not independently confirmed.

reading.body:
Iron Mountain VA-2 is a single building within a multi-building Northern Virginia campus that has published 36 MW of IT capacity. At a typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, this would support roughly 900 racks, though the operator describes this as renewable power rather than total capacity. The building is 221,500 square feet and achieved DCOS Maturity Level 3 certification, which qualifies it for high-security data hosting but does not itself identify tenant workload.

Within Virginia, this facility ranks 24th among 23 locations with published capacity figures, because the campus's four published buildings total more MW than any single facility except three others in the state. Virginia has 1,375 MW of published data center capacity across mapped sites, and this one building represents roughly 2.6% of that figure. The state has 326 mapped facilities overall, most of which publish no power specification.

The operator has announced plans to grow this Northern Virginia campus to nine facilities across two million square feet, starting from the 83-acre core where VA-2 sits. The published 36 MW is renewable power specifically, leaving the building's total IT capacity unstated. Whether this campus will matter to AI scaling depends on whether the operator publishes its full power budget and whether the planned expansion happens; neither is confirmed in available sources.
